source.title: Newry Reporter, 7 May 1936, p. 6 ("Kilkeel Rural Council")
source.publisher: Newry Reporter (via the British Newspaper Archive)
source.check: Read on the page image of the Newry Reporter's list of the Kilkeel (South Down) rural council nominations: no contest in any division; the only new members were Messrs. Grant (Cross) and M'Bride (Kilkeel East).

note: Triennial election of the rural district councillors, one for each of the nineteen electoral divisions. Nominations were received on 6 May 1936 and there was no contest in any division. The only new members were Mr. John T. Grant and Mr. James M'Bride. Polling in County Down was fixed for 28 May 1936. Filed on 1936-06-04, the polling day for county council and rural district elections in Co. Down that year (confirmed); previously filed under 1936-05-28 (verification 5 Nov 2026). Returned unopposed.
correctionNote: Corrected from the page image of Newry Reporter, 7 May 1936, p. 6 (council-audit, Nov 2026): citation moved from 'Belfast Telegraph, 7 May 1936, p. 6', which has no Kilkeel Rural Council article, to the Newry Reporter list it describes; the name is printed there. Name_As_Printed George Annett -> Geo. Annett as printed. The paper prints the division 'Maghereagh'; the 1930 and 1939 returns file George Annett under Maghera. Renamed from 'Maghereagh' to Maghera (w8-redirects, Nov 2026): the Newry Reporter, 7 May 1936, p. 6 prints the division 'Maghereagh' (Geo. Annett), its variant of Maghera: the list has the council's nineteen divisions with Maghera's place taken by Maghereagh, George Annett stood for Maghera in every other round from 1924 to 1946 and held it from 1924 to 1939, and the paper names him a sitting member (the only new members were Grant and McBride); the round's other variant spellings (Attacal, Bracknagh, Foranny) are filed under the divisions' own names too. The old address (maghereagh) answers with a redirect to this one. Re-cited from the page image of the Newry Reporter, 7 May 1936, p. 6 (w8-review, Nov 2026): the page cited before (Newry Reporter, 7 May 1936, p. 6 ("Kilkeel Rural Council")) carries no Kilkeel rural council list; the Reporter's list names every division's member as on file.
